title: Abhishek Banerjee alleges 2 am attack on his Kolkata home; BJP minister dismisses claim
dek: The Trinamool leader blamed BJP supporters and accused police of standing by. Police have not confirmed his claims of stone-pelting and firing.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Trinamool Congress general secretary Abhishek Banerjee has accused BJP supporters of attacking his Kolkata home at about 2 am on Saturday, alleging stone-pelting and firing "right under the watch of the Kolkata police". A BJP minister dismissed his account, and police have not confirmed that stones were thrown or shots fired.

Mr Banerjee, the Diamond Harbour MP, made the allegations in posts on X overnight and said it was "the seventh attempt on my life in the last six months". Police said on Saturday morning that the situation was under control, according to reports. No arrests have been reported.

## What each side says

According to Mr Banerjee's posts and reports from the scene, a crowd gathered outside his residence, which one report placed in the Kalighat area of south Kolkata, after midnight. Trinamool workers alleged that BJP supporters shouted "chor, chor" (thief, thief) at about 2.30 am, that a clash followed, that cutouts and banners of Mr Banerjee were damaged and that several Trinamool supporters were hurt, according to one report. None of the injuries has been confirmed by police or hospitals. Reports said there was a confrontation between supporters of the two parties before police intervened to separate them.

Mr Banerjee came down from the house and sat outside in protest from about 2.45 am to 6 am, one report said, and had a heated exchange with police officers. He went back inside after police asked him to and a Trinamool worker who had been detained was released, according to the same report. He said police and the administration had failed to act, and also criticised the courts: "Thank you, Calcutta High Court and the Supreme Court of India, for remaining mute spectators," he wrote. He said he would post videos of the incident, and shared clips on Saturday morning.

Saturday is Mr Banerjee's birthday, and supporters had gathered outside his home. Panchayat Minister Dilip Ghosh of the BJP, speaking to reporters in New Town, mocked what he called a politician's birthday "being celebrated on the footpath" and said: "If someone creates a disturbance, there is bound to be a backlash." He asked who had "the time to kill Abhishek Banerjee" and accused Trinamool of misleading people. Neither the BJP's state unit nor Kolkata Police had issued a formal statement on the incident by Saturday morning.

## The 'surveillance' complaint

The incident came hours after Mr Banerjee alleged on Friday that "a few unidentified individuals" had been watching his office and residence for two days, and that when confronted they had claimed to be police officers. He posted the registration number of a motorcycle he said they used, asked "who authorised this surveillance and for what purpose", and sought an inquiry from Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the Union Home Ministry, Kolkata Police and West Bengal Police. There has been no public response to that request.

## Background

Relations between the two parties have grown more bitter since the BJP won the Assembly election in May, ending 15 years of Trinamool rule, with Suvendu Adhikari as chief minister. On 29 October Mr Banerjee warned police officers that they would face action once his party returned to power, saying they were framing Trinamool workers in false cases; Mr Adhikari responded by challenging him to contest the 2029 Lok Sabha election from Diamond Harbour. Trinamool has accused the state government of targeting its leaders and offices, and the BJP has accused Trinamool of stoking unrest. The accounts of Saturday's incident could not be independently verified.

## What happens next

Mr Banerjee has asked for an inquiry. Any statement from Kolkata Police on what happened outside the house, and on Mr Banerjee's surveillance complaint, would be the first official account of the night.
